subject: Brightwise launch: forecast, short-term QoS bump, and canary plan
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@brightwise.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Brightwise launch: forecast, short-term QoS bump, and canary plan

Team — quick sync request. Brightwise (contact: Kate) is rolling a major feature next Friday (2026-11-06). They expect a concentrated traffic spike during their launch window: roughly 350–450 RPS sustained for a 20-minute window, with burst peaks up to ~1,200 RPS for a few seconds as clients warm up. Payloads average ~600 tokens per request (mostly generation); total token volume for that 20-minute window is estimated in the attached workbook.

Customer asks (high level):
- Temporary per-customer QPS bump to 400 RPS for the launch window (with an automatic rollback 2 hours after window).
- A 5% canary in prod for the first 10 minutes to observe latency and error trends, then ramp to full traffic.
- Fallback routing to a lower-cost / smaller-context model variant if latency degrades past P95 > 400ms.

My asks for you:
1) Neha — can SRE give a short feasibility check on headroom in the us-west serving pools and confirm whether we need a short reserved burst or if autoscaling + temporary quota change is safe? Also call out any throttler changes required to enable time-limited bump.
2) Marissa — any product flags or routing knobs we should enable for an orderly canary + automated fallback? Any known regression risk if we route 5% of traffic to smaller variant?
3) Monica — CS: confirm customer coordination (client-side backoff, rollout steps) and contact for emergency during launch.

I've attached Brightwise's traffic estimates and a draft canary playbook. Kate is on cc and will confirm final window this afternoon. Please reply with clear yes/no + blockers so I can finalize the mutual action plan with the customer.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@brightwise.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brightwise launch: forecast, short-term QoS bump, and canary plan

Thanks for the clear ask, Dylan. A few clarifying questions from product before SRE jumps in:
- Traffic shape: is the 350–450 RPS the sustained post-canary steady-state or the expected average after ramp? The workbook shows both — call out the conservative number you want us to provision to.
- SLAs: customer expects 99th percentile latency to stay under 900ms; are they comfortable with our P95 target of 400ms during the canary? If not, we should clarify in the plan.
- Caching: is there a chance for prefix caching on common prompts? If yes, token volume could drop significantly and we should recompute quotas.

From product side: we can enable a time-limited quota exception (policy tag: "launch-bump:brightwise-20261106") that expires automatically; this avoids manual rollback. We can also enable automated fallback routing to model-compact-v2 if we see P95 > 400ms for > 3 consecutive minutes during the ramp. The fallback will be a per-tenant routing rule we can stage now.

Risk note: model-compact-v2 changes output slightly for edge cases — we should ask Brightwise to run a small A/B prompt set against it. Monica, can you coordinate a short quality check with the customer?

Marissa
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@brightwise.com
Date: 2026-11-01T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brightwise launch: forecast, short-term QoS bump, and canary plan

Quick operational readout after a brief look at us-west pools and autoscaler curves:
- Current steady headroom for serving pool us-west-1 (gen-instance family) is ~1.5k RPS at current model mix. That gives us margin for the customer's expected sustained 400 RPS bump, provided other big customers don't hit simultaneous spikes.
- Risk: the burst peaks (1.2k RPS) combined with other scheduled launches in the same day could push CPU/GPU contention and increase queueing latency. I'd like to schedule a short reserve window: reserve 1x small reserved slice (equivalent to ~800 RPS margin) from 15:45–16:30 UTC on 2026-11-06. That prevents noisy neighbor problems.
- Throttler change: we can implement a per-tenant temporary quota increase that auto-expires. It requires a one-line config change (policy id) + a deploy-safe rollout. We can have it staged by Thursday EOD.
- Canary config: 5% initial traffic for 10 minutes is fine. SRE recommends a progressive ramp (5% -> 20% -> 60% -> 100%) over 25 minutes rather than a single jump after 10. We'll monitor P95, error rate, and CPU utilization.

Action items I can own:
- Book the reserve slice and add it to the service calendar (ENG-6421).
- Stage the throttler exception as "launch-bump:brightwise-20261106" for QA by Thursday.
- Provide a short operational playbook for the on-call runbook with rollback steps and contact matrix.

Blockers/asks:
- Product: confirm fallback model variant routing name (marissa mentioned model-compact-v2). I need the exact model tag to test routing.
- Sales/CS: confirm exact launch window in UTC and the customer's contact for a rapid escalation (phone/Slack).

Neha
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Kate Liu <kate@brightwise.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@brightwise.com
Date: 2026-11-01T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brightwise launch: forecast, short-term QoS bump, and canary plan

Hi all — thanks for the fast turnaround. Confirming a refined launch window: 2026-11-06 15:50–16:15 UTC (we expect the primary spike in the first 10 minutes). The conservative sustained number for the plan should be 425 RPS; peaks as noted.

We will:
- Enable client-side exponential backoff and a 250ms initial jitter on all deployment clients.
- Run the A/B prompt set you requested against model-compact-v2 and share results by Thursday.
- Have our ops lead (ops@brightwise.com) on-call in case you need a direct line; they prefer Slack for the short window and can accept an emergency phone callback if you provide a number.

Please confirm the reserve slice and the expiry time for the throttler exception (Dylan: you said auto-rollback 2 hours after the window — that works for us).

Thanks,
Kate Liu
Staff Engineer, Brightwise

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kate Liu <kate@brightwise.com>, ops@brightwise.com
Date: 2026-11-01T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brightwise launch: forecast, short-term QoS bump, and canary plan

Summarizing next steps and owners so we have a single action list:
- Neha: book reserve slice (800 RPS equiv) for 2026-11-06 15:45–16:30 UTC; stage the policy "launch-bump:brightwise-20261106" by Thursday EOD; prepare on-call runbook.
- Marissa: confirm exact model routing tag for fallback (please share tag so Neha can test).
- Monica: run the A/B quality check with Brightwise on model-compact-v2 and collect sample diffs by Thursday.
- Kate/Ops (Brightwise): run client-side tests, confirm that backoff will be enabled, and provide point-of-contact on Slack during the window.

Dylan (me) will update the mutual action plan and push the Doc (HubSpot link below) and sign-off. I will also provide an emergency phone number to Kate privately.

Related links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-6421, HubSpot: HS-382719

Thanks everyone — if no blockers, I'll lock the exception and the reserve slice tomorrow morning.

Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
